citeAs: Peng, Y., Shakeel, M., Sudo, Y., Chen, W., Tian, J., Lin, C.-J., Watanabe, S. (2025). OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Proc. Interspeech 2025, 2225-2229. DOI: 10.21437/Interspeech.2025-1062
creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe (Carnegie Mellon University; Honda Research Institute Japan)
description: A cleaned and filtered subset of the YODAS (YouTube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech) dataset, produced by applying a scalable data-cleaning pipeline to the raw YODAS data. The pipeline includes CTC-based resegmentation, language-identification filtering, and CTC-score-based filtering, yielding 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages. This dataset was used to train the OWSM v4 series of open speech foundation models.
inLanguage: 75 languages including en, es, ru, pt, ko, fr, de, it, vi, id, zh, ja, nl, tr, bn, hi, uk, be, gl, ca, and others
name: espnet_yodas_owsmv4 (Cleaned YODAS for OWSM v4)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (transcriptions and timestamps) are inherited from the original YODAS dataset, which sourced them from YouTube. No new human annotation was performed. The cleaning pipeline uses automated tools to verify and filter existing annotations: CTC segmentation for timestamp realignment, fastText for text language verification, and ECAPA-TDNN for audio language verification.
rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced, similar to the raw YODAS data. English constitutes the largest share (74.6k hours), whereas many other languages are underrepresented. The authors explicitly acknowledge this imbalance and note that for simplicity they keep the original distribution without any resampling.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from the raw YODAS dataset, which was originally crawled from YouTube. The raw YODAS data contains 370k hours of audio in 149 languages. The authors applied a three-step cleaning pipeline: (1) CTC-based resegmentation to realign audio and text, (2) LID-based filtering to remove utterances with incorrect language labels, and (3) CTC-score-based filtering to remove low-quality audio-text alignments. The final cleaned dataset contains 166k hours of speech across 75 languages.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw YODAS data: 370k hours of audio in 149 languages, crawled from YouTube. YODAS provides unsegmented long-form recordings, each accompanied by a list of text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. The raw data has not undergone rigorous cleaning and may contain annotation errors including mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text.
rai:dataLimitations: The language distribution is highly imbalanced, with English dominating and many languages underrepresented. The OWSM-CTC v3.2 model used for resegmentation supports only a subset of the languages present in YODAS, limiting coverage. The CTC-score-based filtering is language-dependent and uses a single global threshold (θCTC=0.10) rather than per-language optimization.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The language distribution across the 75 languages is kept as the original distribution without any resampling. English constitutes the largest share (74.6k hours at θCTC=0.10), while many other languages remain underrepresented.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three-step pipeline: (1) Resegmentation — audio and text are realigned using the CTC segmentation algorithm with the OWSM-CTC v3.2 model; long-form recordings are segmented into utterances of maximum 30 seconds; utterances consisting exclusively of non-speech elements (e.g., music) are removed; resulting in 345k hours across 83 languages. (2) LID-based filtering — text-based LID using fastText and spoken LID using ECAPA-TDNN (SpeechBrain); only utterances where the original language label matches both text and audio predictions are retained; resulting in 284k hours across 75 languages. (3) CTC-score-based filtering — utterances with low CTC confidence scores are removed using a relative threshold θCTC=0.10 per language; resulting in 166k hours across 75 languages.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset advances open academic research by providing a large-scale, publicly released, cleaned speech dataset under a Creative Commons license. It enables academic institutions with limited resources to train competitive speech foundation models, reducing dependence on proprietary industrial datasets and improving transparency and reproducibility in speech research.
rai:dataUseCases: Training multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems; training speech foundation models supporting multilingual ASR, speech translation (ST), and language identification (LID); Whisper-style speech model training.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 model (used for CTC segmentation and confidence scoring); fastText language identification model (text-based LID); ECAPA-TDNN model from SpeechBrain (spoken language identification, lang-id-voxlingua107-ecapa)
